youtube.title: JOBST LANDGREBE
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with scientist and author Jobst Landgrebe about the Hugging Face incident that sparked fears of runaway AI, which he argues was simply a model repeating known hacking sequences under instruction rather than acting autonomously. Jobst contends AI can never achieve genuine intelligence or consciousness, describes the infrastructure boom around data centres as a historic bubble and identifies warfare and propaganda, not machine autonomy, as AI's real dangers. The conversation also touches on Germany's political mood amid talk of war with Russia. For more from Jobst Landgrebe Listen to his previous RCR interview with Paul Brennan | How hype shapes power in the modern west Look beyond the headlines. Get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: DR GLEN DAVIES
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Dr Glen Davies about NZ First's new health policy, which Glen says draws together over a decade of research into metabolic health and preventative care. He points to real-world results from his own rural practice, where a third of patients reversed type 2 diabetes and pushes back on criticism of the policy's ties to advocacy groups, arguing that consulting experts is exactly what good policy should do. Discover more from Dr Davies at Reversal NZ Watch Maree Buscke's RCR interview with Julia Rucklidge | Micronutrients for Mental Health in Pregnancy – The Evidence For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson review a week of pre-election coverage, from a newspaper editorial urging voters to move past pandemic-era grievances, to NZ First's health policy drawing criticism for its sourcing rather than its substance. They discuss the value of minor parties as vehicles for advocacy, question the media's selective outrage over political lobbying, and touch on Nicky Hager's new book and its fallout. For more information check out: Julia Rucklidge's Facebook post Alia Bee's Facebook post Paul Brennan's RCR interview with Rob MacCulloch | TOP's tax doesn't add up Antony Albanese's Facebook video Paul Brennan's RCR interview with Winston Peters | A new policy approach to health

youtube.title: IAIN MURRAY
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Hornby High School principal and ACT candidate Iain Murray about curriculum changes, school lunches, and the phone ban he credits with transforming his students' break times. Iain argues education, not restriction, is the better answer to youth social media use, defends ACT's stance against breaking up supermarkets, and weighs in on defence spending and New Zealand's place in a shifting Pacific security landscape. For more from Iain Murray or find him on Facebook For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: CAROLINE WHEELER
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with retired Nelson GP Dr Caroline Wheeler, recently censured by the Health Practitioners Disciplinary Tribunal for prescribing ivermectin during the pandemic. Caroline recounts why she felt compelled to treat desperate patients, the years-long disciplinary process that followed a colleague's complaint and the personal toll of fighting it while caring for her dying mother. She reflects on the broader campaign against dissenting doctors and urges others not to stay silent. For more information and to sign their declaration visit NZDSOS.com For news you can trust, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart discuss the fallout from Macklemore's pro-Palestinian protest during Ed Sheeran's tour, which saw Macklemore depart amid backlash from stadium owner Robert Kraft. The pair reflect on cancel culture's staying power, drawing parallels to their own experiences of professional ostracism and muse on luxury beliefs, the erosion of manners, and whether society is heading toward some larger reckoning. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with Farzin Irani of Sovereignty Capital about the Reserve Bank's expected interest rate hikes, which Farzin ties to currency defence rather than genuine economic strength. He walks through rising diesel costs, the widening gap between rich and poor and the geopolitical pressures building around Russia, Ukraine and Europe's economy, before turning to the scale of global sovereign debt and the risks lurking in bond markets. DISCLAIMER: The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They do not constitute personalised financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Listeners should seek guidance from a licensed financial professional who can provide advice based on their individual situation. For more information visit Farzin's new website Sovereignty.capital – with free resources to help people prepare for the future. Discover more from Farzin on Linktr.ee

youtube.title: LARRY BLAIR
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with energy policy commentator Larry Blair about the strained global fuel supply chain, as Houthi attacks near the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline squeeze diesel exports to Europe. Larry explains why New Zealand's supply looks stable for now but remains vulnerable to price shocks, and discusses soaring shipping costs, potential US export restrictions, and the risks of further Middle East escalation. For the latest energy news get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: SAAD BAHJAT ABOU-CHAKRA
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with researcher and educator Saad Abou-Chakra about his open letter urging parliamentary candidates to clarify their foreign policy positions. Saad argues that selective media coverage skews public understanding of global crises, weighing New Zealand's nuclear-free stance and its role in Five Eyes against the risks of deeper military entanglement. He calls for greater scrutiny of candidates' worldliness and independent thinking ahead of the election. Discover more from Saad Abou-Chakra on Facebook and Instagram For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday
